Optimal.Notes: Bumping textures to Medium and view distance to Medium gives a noticeably better-looking world without a large GPU cost; FSR from 1024x640 keeps the image sharp enough on the 1280x800 screen. This is the best balance of playability and visual quality the Deck can realistically sustain in SCUM.

profiles.Summary: SCUM is a demanding open-world survival game whose recommended GPU (RTX 2060) far exceeds the Steam Deck's RDNA 2 equivalent (roughly GTX 1050 Ti class), making it a tough fit; expect 25–35 fps at low settings with FSR upscaling. The game is officially Unsupported on Steam Deck, and with no player reports available, all profiles are estimates based on PC requirements and hardware comparison.
profiles.BasisNote: No Steam Deck or ProtonDB player reports were available for SCUM; all profiles are estimated from the PC minimum/recommended requirements and Steam Deck hardware capabilities. On your first run, check the frame rate in an open outdoor area (the worst-case scenario) and drop to Max Battery settings or reduce View Distance further if it stays below 25 fps.

MaxBattery.Notes: Render at 960x600 with FSR upscaling to reduce GPU load significantly; a hard 30 fps cap matched to 40 Hz refresh keeps pacing smooth and power draw low. Expect dips below 30 in dense forests or during heavy PvP encounters.

KnownIssues: No official Steam Deck support — UI, text, and controls may not be optimized for the small screen or gamepad.
Online/MMO gameplay requires a stable broadband connection; latency issues may compound performance problems.
Large open-world environments and dense foliage are likely to cause frame-rate drops and stuttering even at low settings.
Proton compatibility is unverified for this title; some players may need GE-Proton to get the game running reliably.

MaxPerformance.Notes: Uncapping the TDP and maximising the GPU clock squeezes the most frames out of the Deck, but even so a locked 40 fps is ambitious in open areas — expect drops to the low 30s in the most demanding scenes. Battery life will be short, so keep a charger handy for longer sessions.

Optimal.Notes: A locked 40 fps at 40 Hz gives the smoothest feel the Deck can reliably sustain in this game; textures bumped to Medium improve visual clarity without a large GPU cost. Drop to MaxBattery profile on heavily populated servers.

80 GB install size requires a large SD card or significant internal SSD space.
